title: Ars Poetica: the art of poetry in twenty traditions — Greek, Latin, Sanskrit, Tamil, Chinese, Japanese, Korean, Hebrew, Arabic, Persian, Old Norse, Irish, Occitan, Italian, French, Spanish, Portuguese, German, Russian and English

license.payload: Per item, recorded in origin.items. The underlying works are in the public domain in the United States (first published before 1931, or ancient and medieval texts in editions published before 1931), except Sigil's essay, which is the archive's own (CC BY 4.0, by the author). Packagings: Perseus TEI CC BY-SA 4.0; Wikisource pages CC BY-SA 4.0 for the site's contributions; Project Gutenberg texts under the PG licence; Aozora Bunko texts under its terms for public-domain works. The GRETIL Sanskrit files are CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 at the file: handled under the NC payload/record split ruled at EA-CORPORA-02 — the NonCommercial payload licence is carried forward unmodified and does not attach to this seat record. The Arabic Wikisource pages do not name the printed edition they transcribe: edition-level status recorded as UNVERIFIED AT SEAT TIME.
license.record: CC-BY-4.0 applies to this seat record only.

normalization: Originals as fetched under original/ (TEI, Wikisource HTML as served with its revision id, Gutenberg text, Aozora XHTML in Shift_JIS, Internet Archive OCR layers and scans). text/<slug>.txt derived by code: TEI reduced to lines; Wikisource parser output with navigation, edit links and reference markers dropped (several pages of one work joined under '=== <title> ===' headings); Aozora main text with ruby readings kept in 《》 after their base; Gutenberg and OCR text with line endings normalized. No text corrected by hand. Drop capitals set as images or styled initials on Wikisource can fall out of the text layer (Darío's first word reads 'espués').
units: one text file per work; each work carries its tradition as class

cross_references.already_on_the_shelf: Not seated twice: Plato's Ion, Phaedrus and Republic (plato); Aristotle's Poetics (aristotle); Longinus, On the Sublime (longinus); Horace's Ars Poetica and Epistles (horace, 29/02); Ovid's Ars amatoria, Remedia, Tristia and Ex Ponto (ovid, 29/03); Aristophanes' Frogs (aristophanes); Whitman's 1855 Preface (whitman, LG1855); Blake (blake); Dickinson's manuscripts and her letters to Higginson in the Letters of 1894 (dickinson-mss); Langston Hughes's 'The Negro Artist and the Racial Mountain' in The Nation of 23 June 1926 (langston-hughes); the Futurist and Russian Futurist manifestos (futurism); Dada (dada); Pound's essays and Des Imagistes (pound, pound-ii); Stein (stein); Pessoa (pessoa, pessoa-full); the Russian Formalists (russian-formalism); Mallarmé's Coup de dés and Apollinaire's Calligrammes (visual-poetry); Belief & Technique for Telepathic Prose, Make It Human and Sigil's essay in the whole (pearl-and-other-poems; 29/07)
cross_references.beside_eliot: Sigil's 'Tradition and the Individual Seismograph' is seated next to Eliot's 'Tradition and the Individual Talent' by the author's ruling: the essay takes Eliot's historical sense as its tool and turns the poet from recorder into seismograph whose tremors may create the earthquake they register.

queued: Archibald MacLeish, “Ars Poetica”, Streets in the Moon (Boston: Houghton Mifflin, 1926): public domain in the United States; not on English Wikisource, and no scan found this session
Rainer Maria Rilke, Briefe an einen jungen Dichter (Leipzig: Insel, 1929): both Internet Archive copies (the 1932 printing) are access-restricted (lending library), and no other copy was found
Moses ibn Ezra, Kitāb al-muḥāḍara wa-l-mudhākara (the Hebrew poetics in Judaeo-Arabic) and its Hebrew translation by B. Halper, Shirat Yisrael (Leipzig, 1924): no fetchable copy found this session
Zeami, Fūshikaden: no public-domain digital text found (Aozora Bunko and Japanese Wikisource hold none)

scope: Arts of poetry: treatises, prefaces, letters, manifestos and poems about the making of poems, chosen for range — one or more per tradition, from the Nāṭyaśāstra and the Great Preface to the Odes through Mayakovsky, Hagiwara and MacLeish. Copyrighted moderns and contemporary arts of poetry are declared in 29/06 (ars-poetica-wanted).
why_seated: Gathered for the next EA-CORPORA deposit at the author's direction ('an extremely pluriform ars poetica bundle … include telepathic prose'; 'take that extremely pluriform further globally, hebrew, sanskrit, korean'), around Belief & Technique for Telepathic Prose (#1715), Jack Feist's art of poetry, so that the archive's own ars poetica, a deeply serious one that contains and enacts the comic, the parodic and the satirical among almost every other genre, stands among the arts it answers.
ruling: The author's directions of 2026-10-28; 'Tradition and the Individual Seismograph' beside Eliot's by his ruling.
seating: EA-CORPORA-29 (gathered; the deposit that assigns its AXN is pending)
